content.text: Carmen debates Monsignor Lafelle, exposes the Church’s hateful intolerance, and supports the repentant Beaubien after financial ruin, scandal, and Hawley-Crowles’s suicide. In Book 4, Carmen and Beaubien live peacefully in a Bronx bungalow, while Carmen attends the University and joins Father Waite’s group seeking God through spiritual truth. She rejects materialism, disease, death, and evil as unreal mental beliefs, persuading scientists and skeptics. At Ames’s mansion, Carmen and Haynerd overhear Ames bribing Congressman Wales; later she confronts Ames in her Express office. The group transforms the Express into a clean, socially progressive newspaper. Carmen rescues Ames’s addicted son Sidney in her office and brings him home, where weeks of loving care restore him. Father Waite presents their evolving Christian metaphysics and defense of practical healing.
